frozen: 2026-11-02, before the first build, from the locked plan v6 (docs/IRRIGATION_AGENT_PLAN_V6_LOCKED_2026_11_02_EN.md sections 2, 2a, 2c). The terrain threshold, canal-level drops, sizing rule, minimum flows and main canal capacity were written here before any v2 result existed. Change only as a new version.
purpose: Tree-shaped synthetic distribution network for canal_ops_sim_v1 on land types v1.5: the real Lower Hrazdan main canal with synthetic main-canal gates and pump stations, secondary canals with gates, tertiary canals with gates, and parcel groups. Not a hydraulic design, not the real WUA network.

inputs.not_used: SQL archive and every archive-derived layer (point and layer tables, DWG, blocks): owner decision 2 of plan v6, not read at all

zero_canal_demand.GREENHOUSE: reached, no canal demand: greenhouse (possibly wells)

land_types.reached_note: Reached means a canal or pump can deliver to the parcel. It is not 'irrigated': greenhouses and parcels with no crop need have zero canal demand.

locations.fill_missing_from: cadastral geometry representative point (always inside the parcel)
locations.community_attach_rule: community from land types v1.5; for parcels without one, the community outline containing the representative point, else the nearest outline within community_attach_max_m, else '(outside community outlines)'

main_canal.capacity_basis: owner 2026-11-02: 12 m3/s at the Lower Hrazdan head, assumed design value

sections.rule: stage I is split where the cumulative served hectares of its offtakes reach half (upper / lower stage I); stage II is one section

secondary_blocks.min_ha_note: 0.8 l/s/ha x 1.10 x 115 ha = 101 l/s, so every secondary can open at the 100 l/s secondary minimum
secondary_blocks.merge_rule: a (stage, side, window) group under min_ha joins the surviving upstream group on the same stage and side when at most max_merge_gap_windows apart; a small group with no upstream partner takes the next survivor downstream under the same limit; otherwise it stays a small secondary raised to the 100 l/s minimum (merging across longer gaps drew canals across the main canal in the first trial build)

outlets.rule: parcel groups = farm parcels of one secondary block, one 250 m grid cell and one community; outlet point = area-weighted centroid

tree.method: Euclidean minimum spanning tree (Prim, exact) over the outlet points of one secondary block plus its main-canal gate, rooted at the gate
tree.root: point on the main canal nearest to the block's outlet that lies closest to the canal
tree.long_link_rule: a tree link longer than long_link_m (to a remote parcel cluster) always belongs to the secondary canal, never to a tertiary (a 6 km tertiary appeared in a trial build)
tree.cut_rule: post-order: an open subtree reaching tertiary_cut_min_ha (and at most tertiary_max_ha) becomes one tertiary canal whose gate sits on the secondary; every node with a cut or secondary descendant, or with more than tertiary_max_ha of its own, stays on the secondary; open subtrees between two secondary branches of a secondary node are packed in bearing order into tertiaries, and the node's own parcel group joins the smallest tertiary starting at that node (packed or cut from a child) that stays within tertiary_max_ha; a small leftover of single adjacent parcel groups, and a node's own group that fits nowhere, become direct outlets on the secondary
tree.barriers: no tree edge may cross the main canal or a canal of a block built earlier (blocks in key order); a forbidden edge is used only when no other way exists, and is counted
tree.gate_position: a tertiary canal starts at its secondary node; its gate is drawn gate_offset_m inside the tertiary along its first segment
tree.max_levels: main canal -> main gate or pump -> secondary canal -> secondary gate or pump -> tertiary canal -> tertiary gate -> parcels (direct outlets sit on the secondary canal)

terrain.decision_unit: tertiary block (gate cluster) or direct outlet; never a single parcel
terrain.uncertain_band_basis: +-3 m as in wp_core/land_potential.py, fixed here before the first build
terrain.canal_level: canal terrain profile (median within reference_radius_m every profile_step_m) made non-increasing downstream (running minimum); stage II starts at most at the end level of stage I
terrain.main_pump_rule: the main offtake is a pump station when the area-weighted median parcel terrain of the outlets within main_pump_head_m of the gate (along the secondary; else the outlet nearest the gate) lies more than uncertain_band_m above the level at the gate
terrain.label: terrain screening, synthetic
terrain.no_head_figures: terrain differences and canal levels are used inside the build only and are never written to outputs

pumps.unit_rule: smallest unit size with at most max_units whole units covering the station capacity
pumps.override_note: a real pump list ({node, kind: pump|gate, units, unit_lps}) replaces the terrain rule for the listed nodes; ids are kept
pumps.label: terrain screening, synthetic

sizing.rule: capacity = max(P90 of the 2021-2024 dekad gross need incl. downstream losses, 0.8 l/s/ha x irrigable ha) x 1.10, one rule at every level
sizing.need_basis: demand v1 reference 2021-2024 (built on land types v1.4); classes without canal demand on v1.5 count zero; refreshed when demand is rebuilt on v1.5 (plan 2c demand)
sizing.flow_classes: gates and pumps on the main canal and the secondary canals they feed are class 'secondary'; gates and pumps on secondary canals, the tertiary canals they feed and direct outlets are class 'tertiary'; tertiary gates are class 'outlet'
sizing.rotation_note: a parent carries its rotating children's flow: its capacity comes from its own aggregate need, not the sum of its children's capacities

labels.network: Synthetic tree network: real main canal, synthetic gates, pump stations, secondary and tertiary canals
labels.zone: Lower Hrazdan observed zone, stages I and II
